title: Dwight Howard's Potential Return: Warriors to Meet with Free Agent Center
htmlContent:
In a recent development reported by Shams Charania of The Athletic on Twitter, it has been revealed that free agent center Dwight Howard is scheduled to meet with Golden State Warriors officials next week. This news comes as the Warriors continue their search for experienced frontcourt players to bolster their roster for the upcoming NBA season.

Anthony Slater, also of The Athletic, noted on Twitter that the Golden State franchise has been actively exploring options among veteran big men in recent weeks. Howard, a seasoned NBA veteran at 37 years old, is emerging as a genuine candidate for the team. Slater emphasized that Howard's mindset and approach during these upcoming meetings will play a pivotal role in determining whether a partnership between the player and the Warriors will materialize.

Dwight Howard boasts an impressive basketball resume, having been selected as an All-Star on eight occasions and earning the title of Defensive Player of the Year three times during his career. However, after his stint with the Los Angeles Lakers in the 2021/22 season, Howard did not find a spot in the NBA for the subsequent season. In his last NBA campaign, he averaged 6.2 points and 5.9 rebounds in 16.2 minutes per game across 60 appearances.

It's important to note that Howard's playing time in the 2021/22 season represented a career low. At this stage of his career, he is unlikely to be considered more than a situational reserve by NBA teams. However, if Howard is willing to embrace a limited role and potentially sign a non-guaranteed contract, he could be poised for a legitimate opportunity to make a comeback in the league.

The Golden State Warriors have been actively scouting various big men this offseason, including Dewayne Dedmon, Derrick Favors, and Harry Giles, although Giles has already signed with the Brooklyn Nets. The team also expressed interest in JaVale McGee before he ultimately joined the Sacramento Kings.

As things stand, the Warriors currently have 13 players under standard contracts. However, NBA rules stipulate that teams must have at least 14 players on their roster by opening night. This underscores the urgency for Golden State to identify suitable additions to complete their squad for the upcoming season.

The meeting between Dwight Howard and Warriors officials could mark the next chapter in Howard's storied career. As fans eagerly await the outcome, whether this eight-time All-Star and former Defensive Player of the Year will triumphantly return to the NBA with the Golden State Warriors remains to be seen.
